a generalized computational framework for protein–peptide interactions has been developed and that this method is capable of accurately predicting the specificity of a protein–peptide interaction from a protein structure and a peptide sequence.

we have developed a general algorithm for structure based prediction of protein‐peptide specificity, and demonstrated its success across diverse peptide‐binding domains.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a general method for structure‐based peptide binding specificity prediction, and we demonstrated its success across a diverse set for proteins.

we developed a structure‐based algorithm for specificity prediction, which is not restricted to one peptide‐binding family, and we demonstrate substantial success across a diverse set (over 30) of peptide‐binding domains.

we are able to predict specificity of peptide binding for many different types of protein domains, and we are able to do so using a single, generalized algorithm that does not require any input data about the target protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
structure‐based prediction is a promising foundation upon with further development of completely general, de novo prediction may progress.
structure‐based prediction can be used as a general framework for predicting specificity in a wide variety of protein‐binding domains.
structure‐based approaches to protein–peptide recognition can provide a powerful framework for predicting molecular interactions.
